headlines.title: Microchip Technology (MCHP) Stock Looks Like A Bargain On Balance
headlines.summary: Microchip Technology has just seen its share price fall sharply, and the key issue now is whether the current market value still lines up with the cash flows the business can generate over time. With a fresh Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate available, the spotlight is squarely on how that decline lines up with the company’s ability to turn its chip portfolio into sustained cash. The stock has dropped 22.

headlines.title: Here’s Why Truist and Evercore Slashed Their Price Targets on Microchip (MCHP)
headlines.summary: We just published a list of the Analysts Just Slashed Their Price Targets on These 10 Stocks and Microchip Technology (NASDAQ:MCHP) ranked 7th on this list. Wall Street had its worst day in 19 months last Thursday, with chip stocks leading the selloff. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315.

headlines.title: Microchip Technology (MCHP) Stock Fair Value Falls After Analysts Cut Growth Estimates
headlines.summary: Microchip Technology is in focus after analysts cut fair value estimates from US$105.92 to US$86.48, signalling a reset in how the stock is being valued. Recent research points to tighter supply conditions, updated earnings assumptions, and sector wide pressure on valuation multiples as key reasons behind the lower targets. In the sections that follow, you will see how these shifts are shaping the current story on Microchip Technology and what to watch as the narrative evolves.

headlines.title: Microchip Technology (MCHP) Has Two New Robotics And Industrial Network Hooks
headlines.summary: Microchip Technology (NasdaqGS:MCHP) launched the ATFCD52 high speed capacitance digitizer for robotic tactile sensing and grip control. The business added EtherCAT and Time Sensitive Networking support to its PolarFire FPGA solution stack for industrial edge networks. These updates target uses in advanced robotics, augmented reality devices and smart infrastructure systems. The ATFCD52 launch and PolarFire networking upgrades only capture part of what is changing for Microchip today.

headlines.title: Microchip Enhances Robotic Tactile Sensing with High-Speed Capacitance Digitizer
headlines.summary: ATFCD52 device supports dense capacitive sensor arrays, providing detailed tactile data for real-time grip control and early slip detectionCHANDLER, Ariz., Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Reliable robotic manipulation requires more than vision, particularly when handling soft, fragile or irregular objects. Cameras can locate an object, but tactile sensing provides the contact information needed to determine how firmly it is held and whether it is beginning to slip.

description: Microchip Technology Incorporated develops, manufactures, and sells smart, connected, and secure embedded control solutions in the Americas, Europe, and Asia. It operates in two segments, Semiconductor Products and Technology Licensing. The company offers general-purpose 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit mixed-signal microcontrollers; 32-bit and 64-bit embedded mixed-signal microprocessors; and specialized mixed-signal microcontrollers for automotive, industrial, computing, communications, lighting, power supplies, motor control, human-machine interface, security, wired connectivity, and wireless connectivity applications. It also provides analog products, including power management, linear, mixed-signal, high voltage, thermal management, discrete diodes and MOSFETs, radio frequency (RF), gate drivers, safety, security, timing, application-specific standard products, USB, Ethernet, wireless, and other interface products; field-programmable gate array (FPGA) products; and application development tools that enable system designers to program mixed-signal microcontroller, FPGA, and microprocessor products. In addition, the company offers memory products consisting of serial electrically erasable programmable read-only memory, serial flash memories, parallel flash memories, serial static random-access memory, and electrically erasable random-access memory for footprint devices. Further, it licenses its SuperFlash embedded flash and non-volatile memory technologies to foundries, integrated device manufacturers, and design partners for use in the manufacture of microcontroller products, gate arrays, RF, analog, and neuromorphic compute products. Additionally, the company offers engineering services; wafer foundry, assembly, and test subcontracting manufacturing services; and timing systems, application-specific integrated circuits, and products for aerospace applications. The company was incorporated in 1989 and is headquartered in Chandler, Arizona.
